_provenance.note: Vermont citation authorities. Vermont's operative SNAP regulatory text is cited under the Code of Vermont Rules (CVR) convention '13-170-005' (Agency 13, Sub-Agency 170, Chapter 005), commonly abbreviated with an internal 270-280 sub-section range. This pack defines a SECOND citation family, 'vtsa', matching Vermont Statutes Annotated citations (e.g. '33 V.S.A. § 1203a'), since this pack's flagship drug-felony finding rests specifically on a statutory citation, not a CVR section number, and this pack expects both forms to appear in generated answers.

patterns.note: Code of Vermont Rules, Agency 13 (Agency of Human Services), Sub-Agency 170 (Department for Children and Families), Chapter 005 (FOOD STAMPS/3SQUARESVT, 270 TO 280). This pack found the Cornell LII mirror of this citation to be a stale, generic pre-2010s 7 CFR 273 base-rule reprint with no Vermont-specific current figures — see freshness.json before citing a specific dollar amount to this section.
Vermont Statutes Annotated, cited with title and section number, e.g. 33 V.S.A. § 1203a (Application of 21 U.S.C. § 862a — the drug-felony SNAP-ban opt-out, added 2009).

vtcvr.note: Food Stamps (3SquaresVT) (270 to 280) — Vermont's adoption-by-reference of the generic 7 CFR 273 federal base rule; Cornell LII mirror confirmed stale (references 'Food Stamp Act of 1977,' internal effective-date markers no later than 11/1/1998, base $3,000 resource limit with no Vermont-specific COLA update, no trace of the 185% FPL BBCE gate or EITC categorical-eligibility mechanism)

vtsa.note: Application of 21 U.S.C. § 862a — full, unconditional exemption of Vermont-domiciled individuals from the federal drug-felony SNAP disqualification, added 2009 No. 1 (Sp. Sess.), § E.323.2
